cues.text: Good evening, I’m Geoffrey Miller, from the University of Nottingham Student Union.
cues.speaker: Geoffrey

cues.text: And in this week’s free class, Carlos Garcia is going to tell us about safety around campus. Over to you, Carlos.
cues.speaker: Geoffrey

cues.text: Thank you, Geoffrey. And thank you for all of your attendance today.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Also, I would like to thank the student union here at the university for organising this lecture.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Well, I have been serving and protecting the city of Nottingham for over 20 years now as a member of the police department.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Does anyone know what type of crime is the most prevalent on campus? I heard someone say drugs and alcohol - that’s actually isn’t too much of an issue.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Violence? Nope. Actually, the biggest thing we worry about here is theft. The nature of crime on Nottingham’s campus is quite different from that of the surrounding areas.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Crime rates across the East Midlands are very difficult to control.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: We would like to see the rate stay the same for this calendar year, but it has been increasing steadily over the past three years.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: On campus, however, I’m happy to say that the overall crime rate has fallen this year.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: You wouldn’t think so if you have seen the extremely exaggerated stories in the media.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: The media has done nothing but cause more concern about crime in our area.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Even the crime shows you see today are a little bit far fetched, but at least viewers know they are not real events.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: We would really like to see more factual news articles out there so the public can have a rational sense of the safety level of our society.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: OK, let’s move on to what to do when you see a crime.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Do not get involved if at all possible, and do not draw too much attention to yourself by running away in a conspicuous manner.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Though most likely (and hopefully) you will not have to experience this situation, if you are being mugged please do not try to resist.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Instead, be compliant and seek help after the incident.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Like I said, though, it is highly unlikely that you will find yourself amidst a crime, but it is important to be prepared should it ever happen.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: We find that educating students and staff on the correct precautions to take is the best way to increase your safety.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Just remember to be smart when you’re out late at night, and avoid any area or person that looks suspicious. I know it sounds obvious but I cannot stress this enough.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: It is also not a bad idea to have your mobile phone with you at all times, but be careful.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: If you are chatting on your smartphone on your way home, you are a prime target for thieves.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: I’d like to see a show of hands - how many people have left work or the library after 10 p.m to go home before?
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: A lot of you, right? If you do have to go home late at night, please don’t walk home alone.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: More often than not there is someone there that will be walking the same direction as you at some point.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Walk home with a friend or coworker. Even if you must use your phone to call someone that is nearby to walk with you, it is always safer to walk home with someone.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: So when you’re walking home, you may feel more comfortable with some sort of self-defense, such as pepper spray.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Now it’s your call whether you want to carry something like this or not. However, I absolutely advise against carrying a knife or any other offensive weapon.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: All too often they can be used against you if you are disarmed, putting yourself in more dagger.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: For all those interested, the recreation centre offers a free self-defense class to all students every Thursday evening.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: While obviously an introductory self-defense class may not equip you to fight off villains like a regular superhero, it does come in handy sometimes.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: After taking a self-defense class, you will surely be more aware of possible dangers and how to deal with them.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: So hopefully now you have a more complete understanding of the nature of crimes committed on your campus, and how to avoid being a victim.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: I know most students at the University of Nottingham are not the criminal types, but remember that there is no barrier like a wall or something keeping non-students out.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: There is no army force securing the borders, and I doubt anyone wants it that way.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: The campus is generally a safe place, but it is not immune to small crimes once in a while.
cues.speaker: Carlos

cues.text: Alright. That’s all I have to say for today. Stay safe!
cues.speaker: Carlos
